title: One hidden bit per incidence lets a law lay out its own round sphere
subject: Which local laws on knot spaces with two kinds of points have exactly the round octahedral knot spheres as their spheres
conclusion: A local law without hidden states cannot force a round sphere: if it allows the octahedral knot sphere, it allows long capped tubes, whose knot contradictions resolution refutes in bounded width. With one hidden bit per incidence, marking straight seams between digons, a law's spheres are exactly the octahedral knot spheres at every size, so it lays out its own round sphere and a contradiction needing width Theta(sqrt n).
